body:
This PR adds automatic differentiation tests using `ForwardDiff` for a subset of functions which check that soil skin-temperature solve, screen level reconstruction, and snow skin-temperature solve are compatible with automatic differentiation.

I asked a LLM to write a majority of the code.

closes https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaLand.jl/issues/1914
title: Add ForwardDiff tests for surface flux path

## Purpose 
I noticed when looking at some site level runs that the root extraction could sometimes be quite different from transpiration. This could happen if the plant hydraulics parameters are incorrect, so that the canopy is transpiring at a reasonable rate (moisture stress computed from soil moisture), but the water flux computed by applying Darcy's law to a canopy leaf potential and the soil potential leads to something that doesnt extract very much water from the soil (because leaf water potential is very wrong). Then the leaf water content decreases in time, while the plant is transpiring, and the soil isnt losing water. Because the plant has a linear retention curve, things don't break. Moreover, when we compute psi using theta, we clipped theta at zero, so theta was becoming more and more negative without increasing the flux (because psi was capped).

This branch tries out a version where the root extraction ~ transpiration. It is not exact, I think because transpiration is computing implicitly while the root extraction is explicit, but it's a first pass at something more like what we would want in steady state. Because of this, we still make use of a prognostic water content in order to track total water correctly.

Additionally, this PR corrects the field capacity formula. This is the same critical saturation used for bare soil evaporation.  We also introduce a wilting point so that the transpiration can turn off before the soil reaches the residual water content (asymptotically).



## Impact
in 2 year runs:
LHF RMSE drops from 12.0 to 11.6, SHF drops from 11.4 to 11.0, including in improvements in the Amazon basin.
This PR also improves our T/ET partitioning from ~50% to ~55%.

in 19 year run: https://buildkite.com/clima/climaland-long-runs/builds/5153 vs the main run the previous day: 
RMSE on LHF drops from to 11.5 10.7; SHF: to 11 to 10.2, and the partitioning of the bowen ratio looks improved: RMSE is unchanged but the seasonal cycle looks much better (Partioning leaderboard).
